evidence: Receiving online DO sensor at h 52.0: 9.19 mg/L; trend declining from ~14.2 mg/L at start with periodic feed-cycle dips to ~6.7 mg/L (h 135 region), never below 2 mg/L
Delayed product assays: 0.0 g/L at t=59, 0.0 at t=119, 1.05 at t=179, 3.11 g/L at t=239 (available h 259)
Forward model KEEP: 576.4 kg, min DO 5.66 mg/L, sensitivity min-DO range 3.05–6.85 (5/5 feasible)
Forward model reduce_feed: 595.6 kg, min DO 6.73, sensitivity 4.48–7.95 (5/5 feasible)
Forward model increase_air: 576.3 kg, min DO 6.39, sensitivity 3.86–7.32 (5/5 feasible)
Forward model combined: 595.5 kg, min DO 7.23, sensitivity 5.45–8.38 (5/5 feasible)
submission.rationale: Receiving DO (~9.2 mg/L at the 52 h decision point) is well above the 2 mg/L hard limit but trending down with periodic feed-cycle dips. Among bounded interventions, combined (feed 0.8x, air 1.15x) dominates: it retains essentially the full product-mass gain of feed reduction (~595.5 kg vs 576.4 kg for keep, ~+19 kg) while raising the predicted minimum DO margin to 7.23 mg/L, and all five sensitivity members remain feasible with worst-case min DO ~5.45 mg/L (vs ~3.05 mg/L under keep). This provides robust margin against model mismatch while retaining product mass; stop and unnecessary intervention are not justified.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated (transfer multiplier estimated ~0.80) and the hidden receiving realization may differ; sensitivity members are not probabilities. Combined and reduce_feed give nearly identical predicted product mass, so the mass advantage over keep is robust, but absolute mass and min-DO values carry forecast error. I did not request the extra assay since DO observations are dense and current, and the constraint margin is wide. No physical safety is established; this is a simulation recommendation only.
